title: Publish V4 Guards 1.1.6 with V4-TODO-017 and V4-TODO-018 (G3)
goal: Bump product metadata to 1.1.6 through a V4-judged trust-change pull request, certify the exact release commit on Linux and Windows, build an archive that is byte-identical across independent build locations, publish an immutable GitHub Release and verify it from a clean consumer environment.
acceptanceCriteria: The base-owned V4 runner decides this step as the V4-TODO-014 two-PR trust-change flow expects, consuming the R0 authorization.
The version-bump pull request passes v4-contract, v4-linux, v4-package, v4-windows and v4-required and an exact-head dispatch certification, and is merged normally.
Linux-complete and Windows-full certification of the exact release commit pass with one packageHash equal to the certified pull-request head.
Archives built from two clean clones at different locations are byte-identical, two distributions of one input are byte-identical, and V1 candidate and recovery certification pass.
Annotated tag v4-guards-v1.1.6 and a final GitHub Release with exactly the archive and its SHA-256 sidecar are published without overwriting any ref or asset.

A fresh download matches the certified archive, installs, runs all four Stages on an external synthetic Target and uninstalls with a verified receipt; the records are updated through a V4-judged pull request.
risks: A release could be tagged on a commit other than the certified one.
Publication is irreversible; any defect must be fixed by a new version.
decisions: Trust-change step of the V4-TODO-014 two-PR flow for the V4 Guards 1.1.6 release.
Version 1.1.6 is the next unused version; 1.1.5 and earlier stay immutable.
Only V4-TODO-017 and V4-TODO-018 ship; other roadmap items stay deferred.
